- Total of 131 athletes won medals at the 1960 Games. So (131 athletes, count, medals) maybe relation "number of athletes winning medals" but need subject entity. Could be "1960 Winter Olympics" -> "number of medal-winning athletes" = 131. Use relation "number of medal-winning athletes". Subject: "1960 Winter Olympics". Object: "131". object_type: quantity/integer.

- Soviet Union was awarded the most medals, with its athletes winning seven gold medals, five silver, and nine bronze, for a total of 21 medals overall. So triplet: (Soviet Union, number of gold medals, 7). (Soviet Union, number of silver medals, 5). (Soviet Union, number of bronze medals, 9). (Soviet Union, total medals, 21). Also relation "most medals" maybe "ranking position" but we can capture "medal count rank" = 1. Could do (Soviet Union, medal rank, 1). But not explicit "rank 1", just "most medals". Might be okay to include "most medals" as relation "most medals" but better to capture counts.

- United States placed second in medal count, with a total of 10 medals. So (United States, total medals, 10). Also maybe (United States, medal rank, 2). Use "medal rank".

- Germany placed third, with eight medals overall. So (Germany, total medals, 8). (Germany, medal rank, 3).

- Of the 30 NOCs competing in the 1960 Games, 14 won at least one medal, with 10 of these winning at least one gold medal. So (1960 Winter Olympics, number of NOCs, 30). (30 NOCs, qualified as "competing" maybe relation "participated in". Could do (NOC, participated in, 1960 Winter Olympics) but need subject entity. Could create generic: (1960 Winter Olympics, number of participating NOCs, 30). Then (1960 Winter Olympics, number of NOCs winning at least one medal, 14). (1960 Winter Olympics, number of NOCs winning at least one gold medal, 10). Also "won at least one medal" maybe relation "won at least one medal" but we can use counts.

- There was a bronze medal awarded to Theron Bailie, USA, for the development of the digital clock used for the first time in downhill skiing. So (Theron Bailie, award received, bronze medal). Qualifier: {"relation":"point in time","object":"1960"}? Not explicit date, but it's at 1960 Games. Could add qualifier "point in time" = 1960 Winter Olympics. Or "event" qualifier. Use qualifier: {"relation":"awarded at","object":"1960 Winter Olympics"} maybe. Use relation "awarded at". But need to follow allowed qualifiers: they can be any relation. We'll use "point in time". So qualifier point in time = 1960 Winter Olympics. Also object_type award. Also reason: "for the development of the digital clock used for the first time in downhill skiing". Could add qualifier "reason" = "development of the digital clock used for the first time in downhill skiing". But not required.

- Also "Theron Bailie, USA" indicates nationality. Could add (Theron Bailie, country of citizenship, USA). But not explicitly stated as citizenship, but "Theron Bailie, USA" indicates representing USA. Could add (Theron Bailie, represented country, USA). Use relation "country represented". We'll include.

- Also "Soviet Union ... its athletes winning seven gold medals..." Could also have (Soviet Union, number of athletes winning medals, ?) Not given.

- Also "A total of 131 athletes won medals at the 1960 Games." Could also have (1960 Winter Olympics, number of medal-winning athletes, 131). Good.
